questions.prompt: The box plots show the battery lives (hours) of two brands. Which interpretation is correct?
questions.prompt_markup: The box plots show the battery lives (hours) of two brands. Which interpretation is correct?

choices.text: Brand A's lives vary more, because its box is narrower than brand B's box is.
Typical lives are the same (both medians 11 hours), but brand B's lives vary more (IQR 4 versus 2 hours).
Brand B lasts longer, because its longest-lasting battery runs longer than brand A's does.
Brand B is better in every way, because its whiskers and its box are both longer.

questions.correct_answer: Typical lives are the same (both medians 11 hours), but brand B's lives vary more (IQR 4 versus 2 hours).
questions.grading_note: Same median; IQRs 2 and 4. The others use the maximum as the center, read a narrow box as more spread, or call more spread better.

questions.prompt: Waiting times at two stores: store 1 is roughly symmetric with mean 6 minutes and standard deviation 1.5 minutes; store 2 is skewed right with median 5 minutes, IQR 6 minutes, and a few waits over 20 minutes. Which interpretation is correct?
questions.prompt_markup: Waiting times at two stores: store 1 is roughly symmetric with mean 6 minutes and standard deviation 1.5 minutes; store 2 is skewed right with median 5 minutes, IQR 6 minutes, and a few waits over 20 minutes. Which interpretation is correct?

choices.text: Store 2 often has a shorter wait, but its waits are much less predictable, with occasional very long waits.
Store 2 always has shorter waits than store 1, because its median is 1 minute lower than the mean of store 1.
The stores cannot be compared at all, because they are summarized with different measures.
Store 1's waits vary more, because its waits are described with a mean and a standard deviation.

questions.correct_answer: Store 2 often has a shorter wait, but its waits are much less predictable, with occasional very long waits.
questions.grading_note: Median 5 < mean 6 for a typical wait; IQR 6 and long waits show more variability. The others overstate, invert the spread, or refuse a reasonable comparison.

questions.prompt_markup: The box plots show commute times (minutes) by bus and by bike for the same group of workers. Which interpretation is correct?

choices.text: Bus trips are shorter in general, because the bus box plot starts at a lower time than the bike box plot.
Bike trips vary more, because the bike box plot is shorter than the bus box plot on the scale.
Both ways take the same time, because both box plots contain the times from 25 to 28 minutes.

questions.correct_answer: Bike trips are more consistent; bus trips take a little longer in the middle and vary much more, including long trips.
questions.grading_note: Medians 30 and 26; IQRs 10 and 4; the bus range is 45. The others use the minimum, overlap, or read a short box as more spread.

questions.prompt: Two classes both have mean score 70 on a test. Class X's scores form two clusters, around 55 and around 85; class Y's form one mound around 70. Which interpretation is correct?
questions.prompt_markup: Two classes both have mean score 70 on a test. Class X's scores form two clusters, around 55 and around 85; class Y's form one mound around 70. Which interpretation is correct?

choices.text: Class X did better, because some of its students scored around 85, which is above every score in class Y.
Class Y has more spread, because its scores are all close to the middle of the range of scores.
The equal means hide a difference: class X seems to contain two groups doing very differently; class Y is more alike.
The classes performed the same way, because their means are equal and the mean summarizes the whole class.

questions.correct_answer: The equal means hide a difference: class X seems to contain two groups doing very differently; class Y is more alike.
questions.grading_note: A bimodal shape suggests two subgroups; the mean alone hides it. The others ignore shape or invert spread.

questions.prompt: Apples from two farms both have mean weight 150 g; farm A's weights have standard deviation 5 g and farm B's have standard deviation 20 g. Both distributions are roughly symmetric. Which interpretation is correct?
questions.prompt_markup: Apples from two farms both have mean weight 150 g; farm A's weights have standard deviation 5 g and farm B's have standard deviation 20 g. Both distributions are roughly symmetric. Which interpretation is correct?

choices.text: Farm B's apples are heavier, because a standard deviation of 20 g is larger than one of 5 g.
Farm A's apples are more uniform in size; on average, apples from both farms weigh about the same.
Farm A's apples are lighter, because a smaller standard deviation means a smaller mean weight.
The farms' apples are the same in every way, because their mean weights are both 150 g.

questions.correct_answer: Farm A's apples are more uniform in size; on average, apples from both farms weigh about the same.
questions.grading_note: Same center, different spread. The others read spread as center or ignore spread.

sections.skill: Judge whether a difference supports a claim

branch.new_demand: Use a standardized difference to evaluate a claim in a report.
branch.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the separation measured in units of spread becomes evidence for or against a reported claim.

questions.domain: Statistics & Probability: Making Inferences & Justifying Conclusions
questions.skill: Judge whether a difference supports a claim
questions.standard_level: Probability & Statistics. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Probability & Statistics, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: A report says that brand X bulbs "last much longer" than brand Y: means 1,010 and 1,000 hours, both with standard deviation 80 hours. Evaluate.
questions.prompt_markup: A report says that brand X bulbs "last much longer" than brand Y: means 1,010 and 1,000 hours, both with standard deviation 80 hours. Evaluate.

choices.text: Weak: the claim would be supported only if the standard deviations were different.
Strong: both brands have the same standard deviation, so the difference in means must be large.
Weak: the means differ by about 0.13 standard deviations, so the lives overlap almost completely.
Strong: 1,010 is greater than 1,000, so every brand X bulb lasts longer than any brand Y bulb.

questions.correct_answer: Weak: the means differ by about 0.13 standard deviations, so the lives overlap almost completely.
questions.grading_note: 10/80 = 0.125. The others overstate or misuse the spread.

questions.prompt: A coach claims the new training "improved race times a lot": median time dropped from 52 to 50 seconds; IQRs 8 seconds. Which evaluation is best?
questions.prompt_markup: A coach claims the new training "improved race times a lot": median time dropped from 52 to 50 seconds; IQRs 8 seconds. Which evaluation is best?

choices.text: The drop is small relative to the spread (a quarter of an IQR), so "a lot" overstates it.
The claim cannot be judged, because the IQRs of the two groups are equal.
The claim is wrong, because a drop in the median time means the athletes slowed down.
The drop is large, because two seconds is a long time in a race of 52 seconds.

questions.correct_answer: The drop is small relative to the spread (a quarter of an IQR), so "a lot" overstates it.
questions.grading_note: 2/8 = 0.25 IQR. Lower times are faster, so the choice saying the athletes slowed down is wrong too.
